record.original_question: A semicopula, also called a conjunctor, is a non-decreasing mapping S: [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] with neutral element 1, so S(x, 1) = S(1, x) = x for all x in [0, 1]. A quasi-copula is a two-dimensional copula-like function satisfying the stated boundary conditions, componentwise monotonicity, and 1-Lipschitz continuity; every 1-Lipschitz semicopula with respect to the L1 norm is a quasi-copula and is 2-Lipschitz with respect to the Chebyshev norm L_infinity. Characterize all associative semicopulas that are 2-Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity. Characterize all quasi-copulas that are exactly 2-Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity, meaning not Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity for any constant c < 2. More generally, for each c in [1, 2], characterize all quasi-copulas that are exactly c-Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity.

evidence.quote: A mapping S : [0, 1]^2 -> [0, 1] is called a semicopula (conjunctor) if it is non-decreasing in both coordinates and if 1 is the neutral element of S.
Problem 7.1. Characterize all associative semicopulas which are 2-Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity.
Characterize all quasi-copulas which are exactly 2-Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity, i.e., which are not Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity for any constant c < 2.
For each constant c in [1, 2], characterize all quasi-copulas which are exactly c-Lipschitz with respect to L_infinity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $[0,1]$ denote the closed unit interval. A *semicopula* (or *conjunctor*) is a mapping $S\colon [0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is non-decreasing in each variable and has $1$ as a neutral element, i.e. $S(x,1)=S(1,x)=x$ for every $x\in[0,1]$. A semicopula $S$ is *associative* if $S(S(x,y),z)=S(x,S(y,z))$ for all $x,y,z\in[0,1]$.

A *quasi-copula* is a function $Q\colon[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that (i) satisfies the boundary conditions $Q(x,0)=Q(0,x)=0$ and $Q(x,1)=Q(1,x)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$, (ii) is non-decreasing in each variable, and (iii) is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_1$ norm, i.e. $|Q(x_1,y_1)-Q(x_2,y_2)|\le |x_1-x_2|+|y_1-y_2|$ for all $(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2)\in[0,1]^2$. Every quasi-copula is $2$-Lipschitz with respect to the Chebyshev norm $L_\infty$, that is, $|Q(x_1,y_1)-Q(x_2,y_2)|\le 2\max(|x_1-x_2|,|y_1-y_2|)$.

For a constant $c\ge 1$, call a function $F\colon[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ *exactly $c$-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$* if it is $c$-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$ but is not $c'$-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$ for any $c'<c$.

Solve the following:

(a) Characterize all associative semicopulas that are $2$-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$.

(b) Characterize all quasi-copulas that are exactly $2$-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$.

(c) More generally, for each $c\in[1,2]$, characterize all quasi-copulas that are exactly $c$-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals general literature on k-Lipschitz semicopulas and quasi-copulas (including characterizations of k-Lipschitz semicopulas and the connection between quasi-copulas, 1-Lipschitz aggregation operators, and fuzzy implicators), but no source directly resolving the specific characterization of associative semicopulas that are 2-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$, nor of quasi-copulas that are exactly $c$-Lipschitz with respect to $L_\infty$ for each $c\in[1,2]$. The status of the problem could not be conclusively determined.

status_evidence.title: Semicopulas: characterizations and applicability
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations of k-Lipschitz semicopulas and related properties are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on k-Lipschitz semicopulas exist but do not directly resolve the posed problem.

status_evidence.title: Lipschitz continuity of copulas w.r.t. Lp-norms
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Lipschitz continuity of copulas with respect to Lp-norms.
status_evidence.claim: General Lp Lipschitz analysis for copulas does not give the specific characterizations requested.

status_evidence.title: 1-Lipschitz aggregation operators and quasi-copulas
status_evidence.snippet: One-to-one correspondence between quasi-copulas and 1-Lipschitz fuzzy implicators.
status_evidence.claim: Background on quasi-copulas as 1-Lipschitz objects, without resolving the exactly-c-Lipschitz L_infinity characterization.
